Q: Using python regular expression to match times A:

Building on @Amber’s solution above, because I had a bit more of a complicated use case:

import re
d = '7 am and 17:55pm 10 january - 7pm 2026 7.00pm time formats may vary 6.55 am - 11:01 pm'
re.findall(r'\d{1,2}(?:\s?(?:am|pm)|(?:(?:\.|:)\d{1,2})(?:\s?(?:am|pm))?)', d)
# output:
['7 am', '17:55pm', '7pm', '7.00pm', '6.55 am', '11:01 pm']

If you want to account for am/AM/Am and pm/PM/Pm I suppose you can either casefold() “d” or replace am|pm with am|AM|Am|aM|pm|PM|Pm|pM .

There is probably a much better way to do this these days, but…

Q: How to remove numbers from string using Regex.Replace? A:

After seeing how much faster a list operation is in replacements, I created a user Class (in VB.Net) named "CKRReplace". The "CKR" prepend is my initials, rather than calling it simply "Replace" (which is used so often elsewhere in VB Code).

    Public Class CKRReplace
      Public Function AllNumbers(strSource As String, _
                                 Optional strReplace As String = "") _
                                 As String
        strSource = strSource.Replace("1", strReplace) _
        .Replace("2", strReplace) _
        .Replace("3", strReplace) _
        .Replace("4", strReplace) _
        .Replace("5", strReplace) _
        .Replace("6", strReplace) _
        .Replace("7", strReplace) _
        .Replace("8", strReplace) _
        .Replace("9", strReplace) _
        .Replace("0", strReplace)
        Return strSource
    End Function
  End Class

Calls to the code to remove all numbers would be from the string "1mir1112211a3bc9" would be something like (again in VB.Net): Dim oReplace as new CKRReplace Dim str1 as string = "1mir1112211a3bc9" oReplace.AllNumbers(str1,"")

The second parameter passed to the oReplace object is not really required since that parameter defaults to "", but I included it for clarity.

Q: How to bold SPECIFIC TEXTS using "TEXTJOIN" or "CONCAT" formula A:

Here's my 2c on this: a combination of UDF and using the Calculate event.

The UDF is designed only to create the input for the code in the Calculate event: it concatenates the various inputs and outputs the final text along with the start/end of each bold section (any input that's a cell and not literal text)

Function MyConcat(ParamArray parts())
    Dim c As Range, bolds As String
    Dim el, txt As String, sep As String, bsep As String, frm As String
    For Each el In parts
        txt = txt & sep
        If TypeName(el) = "Range" Then 'a cell, so flag for bolding
            bolds = bolds & bsep & Len(txt) & "|" & Len(el)
            bsep = "|"
        End If
        txt = txt & el
        sep = " "
    Next el
    MyConcat = txt & "###" & bolds
End Function

The Calculate events scans for any cells using the above UDF and applies the content and formatting to a cell at a fixed offset:

Private Sub Worksheet_Calculate() 'could also use the workbook_calculate event
    Dim frms As Range, c As Range, txt, arr, arr2, i As Long
    Set frms = Me.UsedRange.SpecialCells(xlCellTypeFormulas)
    For Each c In frms
        If LCase(c.Formula) Like "*myconcat*" Then 'formula of interest?
            arr = Split(c.Text, "###")
            With c.Offset(0, 1)               'using a fixed offset...
                .Font.Bold = False            'reset formatting
                .Value = arr(0)               'populate the text first
                If Len(arr(1)) > 0 Then       'any bold text segements?
                    arr2 = Split(arr(1), "|") 'start+length pairs
                    For i = LBound(arr2) To UBound(arr2) Step 2
                        .Characters(arr2(i) + 1, arr2(i + 1)).Font.Bold = True
                    Next i
                End If
            End With
        End If
    Next c
End Sub

Q: MongoDB .NET Update subdocument using Id string with ArrayFilterDefinition A:

This looks like a BSON type mismatch. MongoDB stores the Id field as an ObjectId type, but you're passing a plain string. Even though the values look identical, MongoDB's comparison is type-strict.

You need to convert your string to an ObjectId before using it in the filter:


new BsonDocument("p.Id", ObjectId.Parse(GregsIdAsString))

** EDIT **

based in the context provided, the right parsing is:


new BsonDocument("p._id", ObjectId.Parse(GregsIdAsString))
